Pros:
Eliminates gantry bow caused by differential thermal expansion between aluminum extrusion and steel linear rails — a real and measurable print quality issue at chamber temp
Titanium’s coefficient of thermal expansion closely matches the linear rail steel — this is why titanium specifically, not aluminum
Sold pre-cut by Fabreeko, KB3D, and others — hardware-only installation, no printing required
Widely considered mandatory by experienced V2.4 builders running enclosed hot chambers
Description: Titanium Backers are thin strips of titanium inserted between the gantry’s MGN12H linear rails and the 2020 extrusion. Aluminum expands more with heat than steel rails, which causes the gantry to bow at chamber temperature and introduces first-layer errors. Titanium’s expansion rate is close enough to steel to prevent this. Considered one of the most impactful V2.4 and Trident upgrades per dollar.
Verdict Label: The single most cost-effective V2.4 and Trident upgrade — titanium strips that eliminate gantry bow from thermal expansion
Cons:
Not a drop-in — requires removing linear rails from the extrusion, inserting backers, and reinstalling
Not cheap for what they are — but the price is justified by the improvement
Stainless steel backers exist as a budget alternative but have slightly worse thermal expansion match than titanium
Name: Titanium Backers
